note.explanation: Nucleic acids are built from nucleotides. DNA stores hereditary information, while different types of RNA help use that information to make proteins.
examples: A nucleotide contains a pentose sugar, a nitrogenous base and a phosphate group.
In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine; cytosine pairs with guanine.
note.checkAnswer: Adenine pairs with thymine using two hydrogen bonds, and cytosine pairs with guanine using three hydrogen bonds.
note.simple: Think of DNA as information written in a sequence of bases. RNA helps carry and use that information so a protein can be made.

note.title: Nucleic Acids: DNA and RNA
steps: A nucleotide has a pentose sugar, a nitrogenous base and a phosphate group.
DNA has deoxyribose and the bases A, T, C and G.
RNA has ribose and the bases A, U, C and G.

written.text: What are the types of RNA? Write their functions.
written.finalAnswer: There are three types of RNA: mRNA carries genetic information from DNA to the ribosomes during protein synthesis; tRNA transfers specific amino acids to the ribosomes, ensuring the correct sequence during protein synthesis; rRNA constitutes the structural and functional components of ribosomes.

written.text: Explain the double helix structure of DNA, and discuss the base pairing in this structure.
written.finalAnswer: DNA is a double helix made of two strands of nucleotides coiled around each other. The nitrogenous bases of one strand form hydrogen bonds with the bases of the opposite strand. Adenine pairs with thymine using two hydrogen bonds, while cytosine pairs with guanine using three hydrogen bonds.

written.text: Explain how the information in DNA is converted to RNA and then to proteins.
written.finalAnswer: DNA contains hereditary information in a sequence of nucleotides. This sequence determines the order of amino acids during protein synthesis. mRNA carries genetic information from DNA to the ribosomes. At the ribosomes, tRNA transfers specific amino acids, and their order forms a polypeptide chain, or protein.

example.answer: DNA has two nucleotide strands coiled around each other. The bases on opposite strands form hydrogen bonds: adenine pairs with thymine using two hydrogen bonds, and cytosine pairs with guanine using three.

explain.title: Nucleotides are the units of nucleic acids
explain.body: Your textbook defines them this way: “Nucleic acids are the biomolecules that are composed of units called nucleotides. A nucleotide is made up of three components:” Those components are pentose sugar, nitrogenous base and phosphate group (PO₄).

explain.title: DNA has a double helix structure
explain.body: “DNA is made of deoxyribonucleotides (de-oxy-ribo-nucleotides).” Its sugar is deoxyribose, and its bases are adenine, thymine, cytosine and guanine. The two strands coil around each other. A pairs with T, while C pairs with G.

explain.title: DNA carries hereditary information
explain.body: The nucleotide sequence in DNA determines the order of amino acids during protein synthesis. A segment of DNA that determines the synthesis of a protein is called a gene. DNA is also passed from one generation to the next.

explain.title: RNA helps in protein synthesis
explain.body: “RNA is single-stranded. Its strand consists of ribonucleotides.” These contain ribose and may have adenine, uracil, cytosine or guanine. mRNA carries information to ribosomes, tRNA transfers amino acids, and rRNA forms structural and functional parts of ribosomes.

mistakes: Do not mix up the sugars: DNA has deoxyribose, while RNA has ribose.
Do not write uracil as a DNA base; DNA has thymine, while RNA has uracil.
Do not reverse the DNA base pairs: A pairs with T, and C pairs with G.
Remember the bond counts: A–T has two hydrogen bonds; C–G has three.
Do not swap RNA functions: mRNA carries information, tRNA transfers amino acids and rRNA forms part of ribosomes.
